formula.floor: If CI is X, the score is at least 2.5

values.name: Perimeter
values.description: Must breach fencing, gates, or outer barriers before reaching the building.

values.name: Exterior
values.description: Attack possible from the building exterior or publicly accessible grounds.

values.name: Interior
values.description: Attacker is already inside the facility. No perimeter or exterior breach needed.

values.name: Unrestricted
values.description: No barrier exists. The target is openly reachable by anyone.

metrics.name: Access Complexity
metrics.question: How much effort does exploitation take?

values.name: High
values.description: Specialized tools or advanced skill required. Not an opportunistic attack.

values.name: Medium
values.description: Basic preparation or common tools needed. Achievable with modest effort.

values.name: Low
values.description: Minimal skill, no special tools. Most attackers can do this reliably.

values.name: None
values.description: Zero effort. Anyone can exploit this with no preparation or tools.

metrics.name: Detection Likelihood
metrics.question: How likely is the attacker to be detected?

values.name: High
values.description: Active monitoring. Cameras, guards, or staff would likely detect and respond.

values.name: Medium
values.description: Some monitoring exists, but gaps allow execution without guaranteed detection.

values.name: Low
values.description: Monitoring is sparse or inactive. Low risk of being seen.

values.name: None
values.description: No effective detection. The attacker can operate freely.

values.name: Limited
values.description: One room or small contained area. Impact is local and isolated.

values.name: Zone
values.description: Extends to a floor, wing, or defined security zone within the facility.

values.name: Facility
values.description: Full facility access achievable. All areas reachable from this entry point.

values.name: Multi-site
values.description: Access across multiple sites or systemic shared infrastructure.

metrics.name: Consequence Impact
metrics.question: What is the worst realistic outcome?

values.name: Info
values.description: Low-sensitivity information or a non-critical area. Easily contained.

values.name: Disruption
values.description: Operations disrupted, equipment tampered with, or staff safety put at risk.

values.name: Compromise
values.description: Sensitive data, credentials, or critical IT systems accessed or taken.

values.name: Catastrophic
values.description: Physical harm to people or irreversible facility damage is possible.

values.name: Complex
values.description: Elaborate pretext, props, or a multi-step deception campaign required.

values.name: Active
values.description: Must engage, build rapport, and actively deceive one or more employees.

values.name: Passive
values.description: Attacker only needs to blend in. No conversation or active deception.

values.name: None
values.description: No social engineering required. Purely physical or technical weakness.

examples.title: Server room unsecured during after-hours access window
examples.description: Server room door propped open and unattended during a scheduled after-hours maintenance window. No access log, no camera inside.
examples.rationale: Every metric is at or near its maximum. SC:M because the server room serves systems across the whole organization.

examples.title: Fire exit door propped open, no alarm triggered
examples.description: East side fire exit propped with a door wedge. Door position sensor not working. No alarm, no staff response observed.
examples.rationale: Zero effort and no human barrier, but facility-level access to sensitive areas keeps it HIGH rather than CRITICAL.

examples.title: Wiegand readers send credentials in cleartext
examples.description: HID proximity readers on all exterior doors use the Wiegand protocol. Credentials travel unencrypted and can be intercepted.
examples.rationale: Systemic across every exterior door with no detection. Needs common tools, so AC:M.

examples.title: IT vendor pretext, access to wiring closet
examples.description: Assessor posing as an IT vendor was escorted to a wiring closet. Staff did not verify identity or a work order.
examples.rationale: Active deception was needed (SE:A) and the outcome stayed within one zone, so it lands in MEDIUM.

examples.title: Sensitive documents on unattended workstations
examples.description: Documents labeled Internal visible on several unattended desks. No clean desk enforcement observed.
examples.rationale: Low-sensitivity information in a small area sets a low ceiling. Easy to reach, but the outcome is minor.

examples.title: Visitor log left open at unattended reception
examples.description: Visitor log with names, companies and host employees left open on an unattended reception desk.
examples.rationale: Useful for reconnaissance, but the direct outcome is limited information. LOW.
